mermaid:
graph TB
    %% Styles
    classDef api fill:#a8d1ff,stroke:#2270c1
    classDef core fill:#90EE90,stroke:#006400
    classDef platform fill:#FFB366,stroke:#FF8000
    classDef external fill:#DDA0DD,stroke:#800080
    classDef context fill:#FFD700,stroke:#DAA520

    %% Application Layer
    APP[Application]:::external

    %% Public API Layer
    subgraph API
        PAPI["Public API Interface"]
        GLFW3["GLFW3 Header"]
        GLFW3N["GLFW3 Native Header"]
    end

    %% Core Layer
    subgraph Core
        WIN["Window Management"]:::core
        INP["Input Handling"]:::core
        CTX["Context Management"]:::core
        MON["Monitor Management"]:::core
        VLK["Vulkan Support"]:::core
        PABS["Platform Abstraction"]:::core
    end

    %% Context Creation Systems
    subgraph ContextSystems
        GLX["GLX Context"]:::context
        EGL["EGL Context"]:::context
        WGL["WGL Context"]:::context
        NSGL["NSGL Context"]:::context
        OSMESA["OSMesa Context"]:::context
    end

    %% Platform Implementations
    subgraph PlatformImpl
        direction TB
        subgraph Windows
            WIN32INIT["Win32 Init"]:::platform
            WIN32WIN["Win32 Window"]:::platform
            WIN32MON["Win32 Monitor"]:::platform
            WIN32TIME["Win32 Time"]:::platform
        end
        
        subgraph MacOS
            COCOAINIT["Cocoa Init"]:::platform
            COCOAWIN["Cocoa Window"]:::platform
            COCOAMON["Cocoa Monitor"]:::platform
            COCOATIME["Cocoa Time"]:::platform
        end
        
        subgraph Linux
            X11INIT["X11 Init"]:::platform
            X11WIN["X11 Window"]:::platform
            X11MON["X11 Monitor"]:::platform
            WLINIT["Wayland Init"]:::platform
            WLWIN["Wayland Window"]:::platform
            WLMON["Wayland Monitor"]:::platform
        end
        
        subgraph NullBackend
            NULLINIT["Null Init"]:::platform
            NULLWIN["Null Window"]:::platform
            NULLMON["Null Monitor"]:::platform
        end
    end

    %% Relationships
    APP --> PAPI
    PAPI --> GLFW3
    PAPI --> GLFW3N
    
    GLFW3 --> WIN
    GLFW3 --> INP
    GLFW3 --> CTX
    GLFW3 --> MON
    GLFW3 --> VLK
    
    WIN & INP & CTX & MON & VLK --> PABS
    
    PABS --> Windows
    PABS --> MacOS
    PABS --> Linux
    PABS --> NullBackend
    
    CTX --> GLX & EGL & WGL & NSGL & OSMESA

<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a system design diagram for GLFW, which is a multi-platform library for OpenGL, OpenGL ES, and Vulkan application development.

1. Main Components to Include:

a. Core Library Components:
- Window Management System
- Input Handling System
- Context Creation System
- Platform-specific Implementations
- Event System
- Monitor Management
- Time Management

b. Platform Support Layers:
- Windows Implementation
- macOS (Cocoa) Implementation
- Linux/Unix Implementation (X11 and Wayland)
- Null Backend Implementation

2. Architecture Layout:

The diagram should be structured in layers, from top to bottom:

```
[Application Layer]
     ↑↓
[GLFW Public API Layer] (include/GLFW/*.h)
     ↑↓
[Platform-Independent Core] (src/*.c)
     ↑↓
[Platform Abstraction Layer]
     ↑↓
[Platform-Specific Implementations]
```

3. Color Coding and Symbols:

- Use blue for core components
- Use green for platform-independent layers
- Use orange for platform-specific implementations
- Use purple for external dependencies
- Use solid lines for direct dependencies
- Use dashed lines for optional dependencies

4. Specific Component Details:

a. API Layer (Top):
- Show public headers (glfw3.h, glfw3native.h)
- Include main API categories (window, input, monitor, context)

b. Core Layer (Middle):
- Context management (context.c)
- Input handling (input.c)
- Monitor management (monitor.c)
- Window management (window.c)
- Vulkan support (vulkan.c)

c. Platform Layer (Bottom):
- Win32 implementation
- Cocoa implementation
- X11/Wayland implementation
- Null backend

5. Important Relationships to Show:

- Context creation paths (WGL, GLX, EGL, NSGL, OSMesa)
- Input system connections to platform-specific implementations
- Window system integration with native platforms
- Vulkan integration paths

6. Additional Elements:

- Include a legend explaining the color coding and symbols
- Show external dependencies (OpenGL, Vulkan, OS-specific APIs)
- Indicate optional components with dashed borders
- Show version compatibility notes

7. Implementation Details:

The diagram should emphasize:
- The modular nature of the platform implementations
- The abstraction layer that allows for multiple backend support
- The clean separation between public API and internal implementation
- The platform-specific feature sets

8. Special Considerations:

- Show how the library handles different context types (OpenGL, OpenGL ES, Vulkan)
- Indicate the event handling flow
- Display the relationship with window system protocols
- Include the threading model

Remember to maintain a balance between showing enough detail to understand the system while keeping the diagram clean and readable. Focus on the architectural relationships rather than implementation details.

This diagram should help developers understand how GLFW provides its platform-independent API while managing multiple backend implementations and maintaining clean separation of concerns.

</explanation>
